questions.stem: A team exposes Cilium's Envoy DaemonSet through a Loadbalancer Service with externalTrafficPolicy set to Cluster. What effect does this setting have on routing and source IP?

options.text: The node routes to all endpoints across the cluster evenly, and the node may masquerade the source IP, so the backend pod may not see the source IP.
The node routes only to Pods on the local node without masquerading the source IP, guaranteeing source IP visibility.
The node routes to all endpoints across the cluster evenly and never masquerades the source IP, so the backend pod always sees the source IP.
The node routes only to Pods on the local node and always masquerades the source IP.

questions.explanation: With externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster, the node routes to all endpoints across the cluster evenly. Upstream load balancers expect to be able to send traffic to any node and have it reach a backend Pod, and the node may masquerade the source IP. Consequently, the backend pod may not see the source IP.

optionRationale.b: This describes the Local setting, not Cluster.
optionRationale.c: Cluster does not guarantee source IP visibility; the node may masquerade the source IP.
optionRationale.d: This combines the routing behaviour of Local with masquerading, which is not what Cluster does.

questions.stem: An Ingress object carries the annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb`. Cilium's ingress controller creates the backing LoadBalancer Service for it. What happens to that annotation?

questions.stem: An engineer creates a CiliumEnvoyConfig directly, without going through the Cilium Ingress or Gateway API controllers, and intends it to manage east-west traffic. Which annotation setting should be applied to the CEC?

options.text: Set `cec.cilium.io/use-original-source-address: "false"` on the CEC.
Set `cec.cilium.io/use-original-source-address: "true"` on the CEC.
Leave the annotation unset, because the Cilium agent defaults all CECs to `"false"`.
Set `cec.cilium.io/use-original-source-address` to the pod's original source address.

questions.explanation: The excerpt states that if you create a CEC directly and it is intended to manage E/W traffic, you should set the annotation `cec.cilium.io/use-original-source-address: "false"`. Otherwise Envoy binds the upstream connection pool sockets to the original source address/port, which may cause 5-tuple collisions when pods send multiple requests over the same pipelined HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 connection.

optionRationale.b: Setting the annotation to ``"true"`` is the opposite of the recommendation; the excerpt says all other CECs are assumed to have it set to ``"true"``, which is precisely the behaviour to avoid for E/W traffic.
optionRationale.c: The excerpt says the Cilium agent assumes CECs with parentRefs pointing to the Cilium Ingress or Gateway API controllers have the annotation set to ``"false"``, but all other CECs are assumed to have it set to ``"true"`` — so leaving it unset does not give ``"false"``.
optionRationale.d: The annotation is a boolean-style string value, not a field for supplying an address; the excerpt only describes setting it to ``"false"``.

if the CEC is intended to manage

questions.stem: You are writing a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy that must select the Cilium Ingress proxy itself, so that you can grant it egress to the rest of the cluster. Which endpointSelector expression identifies that proxy?

attachments.title: The allow policy
attachments.body:
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-ingress-egress
spec:
  description: "Allow all the egress traffic from reserved ingress identity to any endpoints in the cluster"
  endpointSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - key: reserved:ingress
      operator: Exists
  egress:
  - toEntities:

The Gateway API removes the need for annotations, which makes resources portable between implementations and therefore lets any developer edit any object.
The Gateway API provides extension points that promote features to API conformance, which automatically scopes Route objects to a single namespace.
The Gateway API centralises HTTP routing, TLS termination, traffic splitting and header modification in a single object that only infrastructure providers may create.

questions.explanation: The excerpt states that the Gateway API is designed with role-based personas in mind and that, by deconstructing the Ingress API into several Gateway API objects, personas gain the specific access and privileges that their responsibilities require. It gives exactly this example: developers in a team could be given permission to create Route objects in a specified namespace without permission to modify the Gateway configuration or edit Route objects in other namespaces.

optionRationale.b: Annotation-free portability is mentioned in the excerpt, but it is a separate benefit and does not grant developers access to arbitrary objects.
optionRationale.c: Extension points and promotion of features to API conformance are described, but the excerpt does not say they scope Route objects to a namespace.
optionRationale.d: The centralised policy mechanism is described, but the excerpt does not say it is a single object restricted to infrastructure providers.

questions.stem: After collecting responses in curlresponses.txt, you count 1221 responses naming echo-1 and 1162 naming echo-2. What does this indicate about the traffic split?

options.text: The responses are more or less evenly distributed across the two Pods
All traffic is pinned to echo-1 and echo-2 is receiving none
The Gateway is failing to reach echo-2, so the counts differ
The split cannot be assessed from Pod name counts

questions.explanation: The counts are close to each other, which is the expected outcome: the reply is balanced evenly across both Pods and Nodes, and the responses are more or less evenly distributed.

optionRationale.b: echo-2 received 1162 responses, so it is clearly receiving traffic.
optionRationale.c: A modest difference between the counts is consistent with an even split, not evidence of a failure to reach echo-2.
optionRationale.d: Counting the Pod names in the collected responses is exactly the documented way to verify the split.

attachments.title: Counts from the collected responses
attachments.body:

 1221
